sentences.zh: 流內九品三十階之內，又有視流內起居，五品至從九品。

translations.literal: Within the thirty grades of the nine ranks inside the flow, there were also quasi-flow court diary attendants, from fifth rank to secondary ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Within the thirty grades of the nine ranks in the regular sequence, there were also quasi-regular court diary attendants, ranging from the fifth rank down to the secondary ninth.

sentences.zh: 初以薩寶府、親王國官及三師、三公、開府、嗣郡王、上柱國已下護軍勳官帶職事者府官等品。

translations.literal: At first, grades were assigned to the Sogdian Treasury Office, prince fief officials, and the Three Preceptors, Three Dukes, open-the-feudal-office, heir-apparent kings, commandery kings, upper pillar of the state and below, protectors of the army, merit officers, and mansion officials of those bearing substantive posts.
translations.idiomatic: At first these grades applied to the Sogdian treasury office, prince fief officials, and the ranks of the three preceptors, three dukes, open-the-feudal-office holders, heir-apparent and commandery kings, merit officers from upper pillar of the state down through protector of the army, and the mansion officials of men who held substantive posts.

sentences.zh: 開元初，一切罷之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, all were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaiyuan era, all of these were abolished.

sentences.zh: 今唯有薩寶、祅正二官而已。

translations.literal: Now only the two offices of Sogdian Chief and Zoroastrian Rectifier remain.
translations.idiomatic: Today only the two offices of Sogdian Chief and Zoroastrian Rectifier remain.

sentences.zh: 又有流外自勳品以至九品，以為諸司令史、贊者、典謁、亭長、掌固等品。

translations.literal: There were also outside-the-flow ranks from merit grade to ninth rank, for the various offices' clerks, ushers, reception attendants, station chiefs, and gatekeepers.
translations.idiomatic: There were also outside-the-flow ranks from merit grade through the ninth rank, assigned to the various offices' clerks, ushers, reception attendants, station chiefs, and gatekeepers.

sentences.zh: 視流外亦自勳品至九品，開元初唯留薩寶、祅祝及府史，餘亦罷之。

translations.literal: Quasi-outside-the-flow also ran from merit grade to ninth rank; at the beginning of Kaiyuan only Sogdian Chief, Zoroastrian Sacrificer, and mansion clerks were retained — the rest were also abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Quasi-outside-the-flow ranks likewise ran from merit grade to the ninth rank; at the beginning of Kaiyuan only the Sogdian chief, zoroastrian sacrificer, and mansion clerks were kept, and the rest were abolished as well.

sentences.zh: 職事者，諸統領曹事，供命王命，上下相攝，以持庶績。

translations.literal: Substantive officers were those who directed all bureau affairs, carried out the king's commands, and coordinated superiors and subordinates to sustain the multitude of tasks.
translations.idiomatic: Substantive officers were those who directed bureau affairs, carried out the sovereign's commands, and coordinated superiors and subordinates to sustain the work of government.

sentences.zh: 近代已來，又分為文武二職，分曹置員，各理所掌。

translations.literal: In recent times they were further divided into civil and military duties, with separate bureaus and posts, each administering what it oversaw.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times the offices were further divided into civil and military tracks, with separate bureaus and posts, each administering its own sphere.

sentences.zh: 五品已上，舊制吏部尚書進用。

translations.literal: For fifth rank and above, the old system had the Minister of Personnel advance candidates.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, appointments from the fifth rank upward were advanced by the Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 自隋已後，則中書門下知政事官訪擇聞奏，然後下制授之。

translations.literal: From Sui onward, secretariat and chancellery officials handling state affairs would investigate, select, report, and only then issue an edict of appointment.
translations.idiomatic: From the Sui dynasty onward, secretariat and chancellery officials in charge of state affairs would investigate candidates, report their selection, and only then issue an edict of appointment.

sentences.zh: 三品已上，德高委重者，亦有臨軒冊授。

translations.literal: For third rank and above, when virtue was high and trust weighty, there was also investiture before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: For the third rank and above, when a man's virtue and the trust placed in him were especially great, investiture could also be performed before the throne.

sentences.zh: 自神龍之後，冊禮廢而不用，朝遷命官，制敕而已。

translations.literal: After Shenlong, the investiture ceremony was abandoned and unused; court transfers and appointments relied on edicts alone.
translations.idiomatic: After the Shenlong era, the investiture ceremony fell out of use; court transfers and appointments were made by edict alone.

sentences.zh: 六品已上，吏部選擬錄奏，書旨授之。

translations.literal: For sixth rank and above, the Ministry of Personnel selected nominees, recorded and reported them, and appointments were made by written decree.
translations.idiomatic: For the sixth rank and above, the Ministry of Personnel selected nominees, submitted a record for approval, and appointments were conveyed by written decree.

sentences.zh: 有唐已來，出身入仕者，著令有秀才、明經、進士、明法、書算。

translations.literal: Since Tang, those entering office by examination were defined in statute as cultivated talent, classics, presented scholar, law, calligraphy, and mathematics.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Tang dynasty, the statutes defined five examination routes into office: cultivated talent, classics, presented scholar, law, calligraphy, and mathematics.

sentences.zh: 其次以流外入流。

translations.literal: Next came entry into the regular sequence from outside-the-flow status.
translations.idiomatic: Next came promotion from outside-the-flow status into the regular official sequence.

sentences.zh: 若以門資入仕，則先授親勳翊衛六番，隨文武簡入。

translations.literal: If entering office by hereditary privilege, one was first assigned six rotations in the personal, merit, and wing guards, then selected into civil or military tracks as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Those entering office through hereditary privilege were first assigned six rotations in the personal, merit, and wing guards, and then selected into the civil or military track as appropriate.

sentences.zh: 選例又有齋郎、品子、勳官及五等封爵、屯官之屬，亦有番第，許同揀選。

translations.literal: Selection rules also included fast-day officers, ranked sons, merit officers, the five grades of enfeoffment, and garrison officers — all with rotation orders and permitted to compete in selection.
translations.idiomatic: Selection rules also covered fast-day officers, ranked sons, merit officers, holders of the five grades of enfeoffment, and garrison officers; all had rotation orders and were permitted to compete in the selection process.

sentences.zh: 天寶三載，又置崇玄學，習《道德》等經，同明經例。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianbao, the Revering the Mystic Academy was also established to study the Classic of the Way and Virtue and related texts, on the same model as the classics examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianbao (744), the Revering the Mystic Academy was also established for the study of the Classic of the Way and Virtue and related texts, following the same rules as the classics examination.

sentences.zh: 自余或臨時聽敕，不可盡載。

translations.literal: The rest were sometimes granted by temporary imperial order and cannot all be recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Other routes were sometimes granted by temporary imperial order and cannot all be recorded here.

sentences.zh: 其秀才，有唐已來無其人。

translations.literal: As for cultivated talent, since Tang there has been no one.
translations.idiomatic: As for the cultivated talent examination, no one has passed it since the Tang dynasty began.

sentences.zh: 職事官資，則清濁區分，以次補授。

translations.literal: For substantive office qualifications, clear and murky ranks were distinguished and appointments made in order.
translations.idiomatic: Substantive offices were classified as clear or murky in rank, and appointments were made in that order.

sentences.zh: 又以三品已下官，及門下、中書侍郎、尚書左右丞、諸司侍郎、太常少卿、太子少詹事、左右庶子、秘書少監、國子司業為清望官。

translations.literal: Also, officials from third rank downward, including chancellery and secretariat vice ministers, left and right assistants of the Department of State Affairs, vice ministers of the various ministries, ceremonies vice director, heir's junior household administrator, left and right junior preceptors, archive vice director, and national university vice rector were classified as clear-prestige offices.
translations.idiomatic: Officials from the third rank downward—including chancellery and secretariat vice ministers, the left and right assistants of the Department of State Affairs, vice ministers of the ministries, the ceremonies vice director, the heir's junior household administrator, the left and right junior preceptors, the archive vice director, and the national university vice rector—were classified as clear-prestige offices.

sentences.zh: 太子左右諭德、左右衛左右千牛衛中郎將、太子左右率府左右內率府率及副、太子左右衛率府中朗將、諫議大夫、御史中丞、給事中、中書舍人、太子中允、中舍人、左右贊善大夫、洗馬、國子博士、尚書諸司郎中、秘書丞、著作郎、太常丞、左右衛郎將、左右衛率府郎將、起居郎、起居舍人、太子司議郎、尚書諸司員外郎、太子舍人、侍御史、秘書郎、著作佐郎、太學博士、詹事丞、太子文學、國子助教、左右補闕、殿中侍御史、太常博士、四門博士、詹事司直、太學助教、左右拾遺、監察御史、四門助教為清官。

translations.literal: The heir's left and right moral instructors; left and right guard and thousand-ox central commanders; heir's left and right commandant office and inner commandant office commandants and deputies; heir's guard commandant office central commanders; remonstrance master; attendant censor-in-chief; attendant of affairs; secretariat draftsman; heir's central approver and draftsman; left and right assistants-in-goodness; groom; national university erudite; department bureau directors; archive assistant; compilation gentleman; ceremonies assistant; guard and commandant office commandants; court diary gentlemen; heir's discussion gentleman; department extra directors; heir's draftsman; attending censor; archive and compilation gentlemen; university erudite; household administration assistant; heir's literary officer; university assistant erudite; left and right supplementation omission; palace attending censor; ceremonies and four gates erudites; household direct examiner; university assistant erudite; left and right memorial retrieval; investigating censor; four gates assistant erudite — were classified as clear offices.
translations.idiomatic: Clear offices included the heir's moral instructors; guard and thousand-ox central commanders; the heir's commandant and inner commandant offices and their deputies; remonstrance master; attendant censor-in-chief; attendant of affairs and secretariat draftsman; the heir's approvers, assistants-in-goodness, and groom; national university erudite; department directors and extra directors; archive, compilation, and ceremonies staff; guard and commandant office commandants; court diary gentlemen; attending, palace, and investigating censors; supplementation omission and memorial retrieval; and the various erudites and assistants listed above.

sentences.zh: 自外各以資次遷授。

translations.literal: Beyond these, all were transferred and appointed according to qualification and order.
translations.idiomatic: All other offices were filled by transfer and appointment according to qualification and seniority.

sentences.zh: 開元中，裴光庭為吏部尚書，始用循資格以注擬六品已下選人。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan, Pei Guangting as Minister of Personnel first used the seniority regulations to nominate candidates of sixth rank and below.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan era, when Pei Guangting served as Minister of Personnel, he first applied the seniority regulations to nominate candidates of the sixth rank and below.

sentences.zh: 其後每年雖小有移改，然相承至今用之。

translations.literal: Thereafter, though small changes were made each year, the system has been handed down and is still used today.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, though small adjustments were made from year to year, the system has been handed down and remains in use to the present day.

sentences.zh: 武散官，舊謂之散位，不理職務，加官而已。

translations.literal: Military prestige offices were formerly called scattered ranks; they entailed no duties and were honorary titles only.
translations.idiomatic: Military prestige offices were formerly called scattered ranks; they carried no duties and served only as honorary titles.

sentences.zh: 後魏及梁，皆以散號將軍記其本階。

translations.literal: Later Wei and Liang both used prestige-title generals to record one's basic grade.
translations.idiomatic: In Later Wei and Liang, prestige-title generals were used to record one's basic grade.

sentences.zh: 自隋改用開府儀同三司已下。

translations.literal: From Sui, Open-the-Feudal-Office Equal in Ceremony with the Three Dukes and below were used instead.
translations.idiomatic: From the Sui dynasty onward, the system used Open-the-Feudal-Office Equal in Ceremony with the Three Dukes and the ranks below it.

sentences.zh: 貞觀年，又分文武，入仕者皆帶散位，謂之本品。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era, civil and military were again divided; all who entered office carried a scattered rank, called the basic rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguan era, civil and military tracks were again distinguished; everyone who entered office carried a prestige rank, which was called the basic rank.

sentences.zh: 以門資出身者，諸嗣王、郡王出身從四品下，親王諸子封郡公者從五品上，國公正六品上，郡公正六品下，縣公從六品上，侯正七品上，伯正七品下，子從七品上，男從七品下。

translations.literal: Those entering by hereditary privilege: heir-apparent kings and commandery kings, secondary fourth rank, lower grade; princes' sons enfeoffed as commandery dukes, secondary fifth rank, upper grade; state dukes, primary sixth rank, upper grade; commandery dukes, primary sixth rank, lower grade; county dukes, secondary sixth rank, upper grade; marquises, primary seventh rank, upper grade; earls, primary seventh rank, lower grade; viscounts, secondary seventh rank, upper grade; barons, secondary seventh rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: Those entering through hereditary privilege began at secondary fourth rank, lower grade for heir-apparent and commandery kings; secondary fifth rank, upper grade for princes' sons enfeoffed as commandery dukes; primary sixth rank, upper or lower grade for state and commandery dukes; secondary sixth rank, upper grade for county dukes; and the seventh-rank grades for marquis, earl, viscount, and baron in descending order.

sentences.zh: 皇帝緦麻以上親、皇太后周親出身六品上。

translations.literal: The emperor's relatives in the fine-hemp mourning grade and above, and the empress dowager's relatives within five degrees of mourning, entered at primary sixth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's relatives within the fine-hemp mourning circle and the empress dowager's relatives within five degrees of mourning entered at primary sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 皇太后大功親、皇后周親從六品上。

translations.literal: The empress dowager's relatives in the major mourning grade and the empress's relatives within five degrees entered at secondary sixth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager's relatives in the major mourning grade and the empress's relatives within five degrees of mourning entered at secondary sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 皇帝袒免親、皇太后小功緦麻親、皇后大功親正七品上。

translations.literal: The emperor's relatives in the bared-shoulder mourning grade, the empress dowager's relatives in minor and fine-hemp mourning, and the empress's relatives in major mourning entered at primary seventh rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's bared-shoulder relatives, the empress dowager's minor- and fine-hemp relatives, and the empress's major-mourning relatives entered at primary seventh rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 皇后小功緦麻親、皇太子妃周親從七品上。

translations.literal: The empress's relatives in minor and fine-hemp mourning and the crown princess's relatives within five degrees entered at secondary seventh rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's minor- and fine-hemp relatives and the crown princess's relatives within five degrees of mourning entered at secondary seventh rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 其外戚各依服屬降宗親二階敘。

translations.literal: For affinal kin, each was ranked two grades lower than the corresponding imperial relative, according to mourning obligation.
translations.idiomatic: Affinal kin were ranked two grades lower than the corresponding imperial relative, according to their mourning obligations.

sentences.zh: 諸娶郡主者出身六品上，娶縣主者正七品上，郡主子出身從七品上。

translations.literal: Those who married commandery princesses entered at primary sixth rank, upper grade; those who married county princesses, primary seventh rank, upper grade; sons of commandery princesses, secondary seventh rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Men who married commandery princesses entered at primary sixth rank, upper grade; those who married county princesses at primary seventh rank, upper grade; and sons of commandery princesses at secondary seventh rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 縣主子從八品上。

translations.literal: Sons of county princesses, secondary eighth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of county princesses entered at secondary eighth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 一品子正七品上，二品子正七品下，三品子從七品上，從三品子從七品下，正四品子正八品上，從四品子正八品下，正五品子從八品上，從五品及國公子從八品下。

translations.literal: First-rank sons, primary seventh rank, upper grade; second-rank sons, primary seventh rank, lower grade; third-rank sons, secondary seventh rank, upper grade; secondary third-rank sons, secondary seventh rank, lower grade; primary fourth-rank sons, primary eighth rank, upper grade; secondary fourth-rank sons, primary eighth rank, lower grade; primary fifth-rank sons, secondary eighth rank, upper grade; secondary fifth-rank sons and state dukes' sons, secondary eighth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: Sons were ranked by their fathers' grade: first-rank fathers' sons at primary seventh rank, upper grade; second-rank at primary seventh, lower; third-rank at secondary seventh, upper; secondary third-rank at secondary seventh, lower; primary fourth-rank at primary eighth, upper; secondary fourth-rank at primary eighth, lower; primary fifth-rank at secondary eighth, upper; and secondary fifth-rank sons and state dukes' sons at secondary eighth, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 三品以上廕曾孫，五品以上廕孫。

translations.literal: For third rank and above, great-grandsons were privileged; for fifth rank and above, grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the third rank and above could extend privilege to great-grandsons; those of the fifth rank and above, to grandsons.

sentences.zh: 孫降子一等，曾孫降孫一等。

translations.literal: Grandsons were one grade lower than sons; great-grandsons one grade lower than grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: Grandsons were ranked one grade lower than sons, and great-grandsons one grade lower than grandsons.

sentences.zh: 諸秀才出身，上上第，正八品上；

translations.literal: For cultivated talent entrants, highest of the highest grade, primary eighth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: Cultivated talent entrants of the highest of the highest grade entered at primary eighth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 上中第，正八品下；

translations.literal: highest of the middle grade, primary eighth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: the highest of the middle grade at primary eighth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 上下第，從九品上。

translations.literal: highest of the lower grade, secondary ninth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: and the highest of the lower grade at secondary ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 明經出身，上上第，從八品下；

translations.literal: For classics entrants, highest of the highest grade, secondary eighth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: Classics entrants of the highest of the highest grade entered at secondary eighth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 上中第，從九品上。

translations.literal: highest of the middle grade, secondary ninth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: the highest of the middle grade at secondary ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 進士、明法出身，甲第，從九品上；

translations.literal: For presented scholar and law entrants, first class, secondary ninth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: Presented scholar and law entrants of the first class entered at secondary ninth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 乙第，從九品下。

translations.literal: second class, secondary ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and those of the second class at secondary ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 若通二經已外，每一經加一等。

translations.literal: If one mastered more than two classics, each additional classic raised the grade by one level.
translations.idiomatic: If a candidate mastered more than two classics, each additional classic raised his entry grade by one level.

sentences.zh: 勳官預文武選者，上柱國正六品上敘，以下遞降一階。

translations.literal: Merit officers competing in civil or military selection: upper pillar of the state ranked at primary sixth rank, upper grade, with each lower title one grade down.
translations.idiomatic: Merit officers competing in the civil or military selection began at primary sixth rank, upper grade for upper pillar of the state, with each lower merit title one grade below.

sentences.zh: 凡入仕之後，遷代則以四考為限。

translations.literal: After entering office, transfers and replacements were limited to four merit reviews.
translations.idiomatic: After entering office, promotions and transfers were assessed in cycles of four merit reviews.

sentences.zh: 四考中中，進年勞一階敘。

translations.literal: If all four reviews were middle-middle, one grade was advanced for years of service.
translations.idiomatic: If all four reviews were rated middle-middle, one grade was advanced for years of service.

sentences.zh: 每一考中上，進一階；

translations.literal: for each review of middle-upper, one grade was advanced;
translations.idiomatic: Each review rated middle-upper advanced one grade;

sentences.zh: 一考上下，進二階。

translations.literal: one review of upper-lower advanced two grades.
translations.idiomatic: and one review rated upper-lower advanced two grades.

sentences.zh: 五品已上非恩制所加，更無進之令。

translations.literal: For fifth rank and above, unless added by grace edict, there was no further rule for advancement.
translations.idiomatic: For the fifth rank and above, unless promotion came through a grace edict, no further advancement rule applied.

sentences.zh: 自武德至乾封，未有泛階之恩。

translations.literal: From Wude to Qianfeng, there was no grace of universal grade advancement.
translations.idiomatic: From the Wude era through Qianfeng, there was no general grace promotion for all officials.

sentences.zh: 應入三品者，皆以恩舊特拜，入五品者多依選敘，計階至朝散大夫已上，奏取進止，每年量多少進敘。

translations.literal: Those due to enter third rank were all specially appointed by grace for old service; entry into fifth rank mostly followed selection and seniority. When grades reached court disbursement master and above, memorials were submitted for imperial decision, and each year a measured number were advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Those due to enter the third rank were specially appointed by grace for long service; entry into the fifth rank mostly followed selection and seniority. When an official's grade reached court disbursement master or above, a memorial was submitted for imperial approval, and each year a measured number were advanced.

sentences.zh: 餘並依本品授官。

translations.literal: The rest all received substantive offices according to their basic rank.
translations.idiomatic: All others received substantive offices according to their basic rank.

sentences.zh: 若滿三計至，即一切聽入。

translations.literal: If one completed three full review cycles, entry was permitted in all cases.
translations.idiomatic: If an official completed three full review cycles, he was permitted to advance in all cases.

sentences.zh: 至乾封元年，文武普加二階。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianfeng, civil and military officials universally received two grades.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianfeng (666), all civil and military officials universally received a two-grade promotion.

sentences.zh: 永淳元年二月敕：「文武官累積勞效，計至五品。

translations.literal: An edict of the second month of the first year of Yongchun: "When civil and military officials accumulate merit and reach the fifth rank,
translations.idiomatic: An edict of the second month of the first year of Yongchun (682) declared: "When civil and military officials accumulate merit and reach the fifth rank,

sentences.zh: 一計至者，多未甄擢。

translations.literal: those who reach it in one review cycle are mostly not selected and promoted.
translations.idiomatic: those who reach it in one review cycle are mostly not selected and promoted.

sentences.zh: 再計至者，隨例必升，賢愚一貫。

translations.literal: those who reach it in two cycles are promoted by rule without exception, wise and foolish alike.
translations.idiomatic: Those who reach it in two cycles are promoted by rule without exception, whether capable or not.

sentences.zh: 自今已後，一計至已上，有在官清慎，狀跡灼然，材堪應務者，所司具狀錄奏，當與進階。

translations.literal: From now on, for those who reach it in one cycle or more, if while in office they are pure and cautious, their conduct clearly excellent, and their talent fit for duty, the responsible office shall submit a detailed report for advancement.
translations.idiomatic: From now on, for those who reach the fifth rank in one cycle or more, if they prove pure and cautious in office, their conduct clearly excellent, and their talent fit for duty, the responsible office shall submit a detailed report and they shall receive advancement.

sentences.zh: 若公正無聞，循默自守，及未經任州縣官者，雖頻經計至，不在加階之限。

translations.literal: If fair conduct is unheard of, they follow routine in silence, or have never served as prefectural or county officials, then even if they frequently reach the threshold, they are not within the limit for grade advancement.
translations.idiomatic: If fair conduct is unheard of, they merely follow routine in silence, or have never served as prefectural or county officials, then even if they frequently reach the threshold, they are not eligible for grade advancement.

sentences.zh: 即為恆例。

translations.literal: This shall be the standing rule.
translations.idiomatic: This shall be the standing rule.

sentences.zh: 」弘道元年，又普加一階。

translations.literal: " In the first year of Hongdao, one grade was again universally added.
translations.idiomatic: " In the first year of Hongdao (683), one grade was again added for all officials.

sentences.zh: 乃有九品職事及三衛階高者，併入五品。

translations.literal: Thus ninth-rank substantive officers and those of the Three Guards with high grades were merged into the fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: As a result, ninth-rank substantive officers and high-grade members of the Three Guards were swept up into the fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 則天朝，泛階漸多，始令仕經八考，職事六品者許入。

translations.literal: In the Wu Zetian reign, universal grade promotions grew frequent; it was first ordered that after eight merit reviews, those holding sixth-rank substantive posts were permitted entry.
translations.idiomatic: During Wu Zetian's reign, general promotions became increasingly common; it was first ordered that after eight merit reviews, holders of sixth-rank substantive posts were permitted to advance.

sentences.zh: 萬歲通天元年敕：「自今已後，文武官加階應入五品者，並取出身，已曆十二考已上，進階之時，見居六品官。

translations.literal: An edict of the first year of Wansui Tongtian: "From now on, for civil and military officials whose grade advancement should enter the fifth rank, all must take account of origin; they must have completed twelve or more reviews, and at the time of advancement must hold a sixth-rank substantive post.
translations.idiomatic: An edict of the first year of Wansui Tongtian (696) declared: "From now on, civil and military officials whose grade advancement should bring them into the fifth rank must meet origin requirements, have completed twelve or more merit reviews, and at the time of advancement hold a sixth-rank substantive post.

sentences.zh: 其應入三品人，出身已二十五考以上，進階見居三品官。

translations.literal: Those due to enter the third rank must have an origin record of twenty-five or more reviews, and at advancement must hold a third-rank substantive post.
translations.idiomatic: Those due to enter the third rank must have completed twenty-five or more merit reviews from their origin grade, and at advancement must hold a third-rank substantive post.

sentences.zh: 」無幾，入五品又加至十六考。

translations.literal: " Before long, entry into the fifth rank was further raised to sixteen reviews.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long, the requirement for entry into the fifth rank was further raised to sixteen reviews.

sentences.zh: 神功元年制「勳官、品子、流外國官出身，不得任清資要官。

translations.literal: A regulation of the first year of Shengong: "Those entering from merit officer, ranked son, or outside-the-flow foreign-office origins may not hold clear-qualification key offices.
translations.idiomatic: A regulation of the first year of Shengong (698) stated: "Those entering from merit officer, ranked son, or outside-the-flow foreign-office origins may not hold clear-qualification key offices.

sentences.zh: 應入三品，不得進階」。

translations.literal: Those due to enter the third rank may not advance in grade."
translations.idiomatic: And those due to enter the third rank may not advance in grade."

sentences.zh: 開元已來，伎術者經二十考，三省都事及主事、錄事十八考，亦聽敘。

translations.literal: Since Kaiyuan, technical specialists after twenty reviews, and chief clerks, clerks, and recorders of the Three Departments after eighteen reviews, were also permitted advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Kaiyuan era, technical specialists after twenty reviews, and the chief clerks, clerks, and recorders of the Three Departments after eighteen reviews, were also permitted to advance.

sentences.zh: 吏部檢歷任階考，判成錄奏。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel examined past grades and reviews, rendered judgment, recorded, and reported.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel examined past grades and reviews, rendered its judgment, recorded the results, and submitted a memorial.

sentences.zh: 每制之日，應入三品五品者，皆令人參趁。

translations.literal: On each day an edict was issued, those due to enter the third or fifth rank all had people attend and press their cases.
translations.idiomatic: On each day an edict was issued, candidates due to enter the third or fifth rank all sent representatives to press their cases.

sentences.zh: 或是遠方牧宰、諸司閒職，齎持金帛贈遣主典，知加階令史，乃有受納萬數者。

translations.literal: Some were distant regional governors or idle-office holders who brought gold and silk as gifts to the chief clerks and the clerks who handled grade advancement — some accepted tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Some were distant regional governors or holders of idle offices who brought gold and silk as gifts to the chief clerks and the clerks who handled grade advancement, and some accepted sums in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 台省要職，以加位為榮，亦有遣主典錢帛者。

translations.literal: Key posts in the terrace offices regarded grade advancement as an honor, and some also sent money and silk to the chief clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Key posts in the censorate and secretariat regarded grade advancement as an honor, and some also sent money and silk to the chief clerks.

sentences.zh: 舊例，開府及特進，雖不職事，皆給俸祿，預朝會，行立在於本品之次。

translations.literal: By old precedent, open-the-feudal-office and special advancement, though without substantive duties, all received salary, attended court assemblies, and stood in procession next below their basic rank.
translations.idiomatic: By old precedent, holders of open-the-feudal-office and special advancement, though they held no substantive duties, all received salary, attended court assemblies, and stood in procession immediately below their basic rank.

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫已下，朝散大夫已上，衣服依本品，無祿俸，不預朝會。

translations.literal: From master of splendid happiness downward to court disbursement master upward, dress followed the basic rank, but there was no salary and no attendance at court assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: From master of splendid happiness down through court disbursement master, dress followed the basic rank, but there was no salary and no attendance at court assemblies.

sentences.zh: 朝議郎已下，黃衣執笏，於吏部分番上下承使及親驅使，甚為猥賤。

translations.literal: From court discussion gentleman downward, in yellow robes holding tablets, they rotated shifts at the Ministry of Personnel to receive orders and personal errands — most base and mean.
translations.idiomatic: From court discussion gentleman downward, officials wore yellow robes and held tablets, rotating shifts at the Ministry of Personnel to run errands and personal commissions — a most base and demeaning duty.

sentences.zh: 每當上之時，至有為主事令史守扃鑰執鞭帽者。

translations.literal: Whenever they reported for duty, some even guarded keys for chief clerks and clerks or carried whips and hats for them.
translations.idiomatic: When they reported for duty, some even guarded keys for the chief clerks or carried their whips and hats.

sentences.zh: 兩番已上，則隨番許簡，通時務者始令參選。

translations.literal: After two rotations or more, they were permitted selection with their rotation; only those versed in current affairs were then allowed to compete in selection.
translations.idiomatic: After two rotations or more, they became eligible for selection with their cohort; only those versed in current affairs were then permitted to compete in the selection process.

sentences.zh: 一登職事已後，雖官有代滿，即不復番上。

translations.literal: Once they gained a substantive post, even when the office term expired, they no longer reported for rotation duty.
translations.idiomatic: Once they gained a substantive post, they no longer reported for rotation duty, even when their term in office expired.

sentences.zh: 勳官者，出於周、齊交戰之際。

translations.literal: Merit officers originated in the era when Zhou and Qi were at war.
translations.idiomatic: Merit officers originated in the era when Northern Zhou and Northern Qi were at war.

sentences.zh: 本以酬戰士，其後漸及朝流。

translations.literal: They were originally to reward warriors; later they gradually extended to court officials.
translations.idiomatic: They were originally meant to reward warriors, but later gradually extended to court officials as well.

sentences.zh: 階爵之外，更為節級。

translations.literal: Beyond grades and enfeoffments, they became an additional tier of ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond grades and enfeoffments, they became an additional tier of honors.

sentences.zh: 周置上開府儀同三司、開府儀同三司、上儀同三司、儀同三司等十一號。

translations.literal: Zhou established eleven titles including Superior Open-the-Feudal-Office Equal in Ceremony with the Three Dukes, Open-the-Feudal-Office Equal in Ceremony with the Three Dukes, Superior Equal in Ceremony with the Three Dukes, and Equal in Ceremony with the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou established eleven titles including Superior and ordinary Open-the-Feudal-Office Equal in Ceremony with the Three Dukes and Superior and ordinary Equal in Ceremony with the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝因周之舊，更增損之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui followed Zhou precedent and further added and reduced them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui followed Zhou precedent and further revised the system.

sentences.zh: 有上柱國、柱國、上大將軍、大將軍、上開府儀同三司、開府儀同三司，上儀同三司、儀同三司，大都督、帥都督、都督，起正二品至七品，總十一等，用賞勳勞。

translations.literal: There were upper pillar of the state, pillar of the state, superior grand general, grand general, superior and ordinary open-the-feudal-office equal in ceremony with the three dukes, superior and ordinary equal in ceremony with the three dukes, great commander, leading commander, and commander — from primary second rank to seventh rank, eleven grades in all, used to reward merit and service.
translations.idiomatic: The titles were upper and ordinary pillar of the state, superior and grand general, superior and ordinary open-the-feudal-office and equal-in-ceremony-with-the-three-dukes ranks, and great, leading, and ordinary commander — from primary second rank through seventh rank, eleven grades in all, used to reward merit and service.

sentences.zh: 煬帝又改為左光祿大夫、右光祿大夫、金紫光祿大夫、銀青光祿大夫、正議大夫、朝請大夫、朝散大夫、建節奮武尉、宣惠尉十一等，以代都督已上。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang further changed them to left and right masters of splendid happiness, gold-seal and silver-seal masters of splendid happiness, regular counsel master, court invitation master, court disbursement master, establishment-of-festival valiant martial commandant, and proclaimer of favor commandant — eleven grades — to replace commander and above.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang further replaced them with eleven grades from left and right master of splendid happiness through court disbursement master, plus establishment-of-festival valiant martial commandant and proclaimer of favor commandant, in place of commander and the ranks above it.

sentences.zh: 又增置綏德、懷仁、守義、奉誠、立信等五尉，以至從九品。

translations.literal: He also added five commandants: Pacifying Virtue, Cherishing Benevolence, Keeping Righteousness, Offering Sincerity, and Establishing Trust — down to secondary ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: He also added five commandants—Pacifying Virtue, Cherishing Benevolence, Keeping Righteousness, Offering Sincerity, and Establishing Trust—extending down to the secondary ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 武德初，雜用隋制，至七年頒令，定用上柱國、柱國、上大將軍、大將軍、上輕車都尉、輕車都尉、上騎都尉、騎都尉、驍騎尉、飛騎尉、雲騎尉、武騎尉，凡十二等，起正二品，至從七品。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude, Sui practice was used in mixed fashion; in the seventh year a code was promulgated fixing twelve grades: upper pillar of the state, pillar of the state, superior grand general, grand general, superior and ordinary commandants of light chariots, superior and ordinary commandants of cavalry, and commandants of valiant, flying, cloud, and martial cavalry — from primary second rank to secondary seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wude the Sui system was used in mixed fashion; in the seventh year a code fixed twelve merit grades from upper pillar of the state through commandants of valiant, flying, cloud, and martial cavalry, ranging from primary second rank to secondary seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十一年，改上大將軍為上護軍，大將軍為護軍，自外不改，行之至今。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhenguan, superior grand general was changed to superior protector of the army and grand general to protector of the army; the rest were unchanged, and this has been used to the present.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Zhenguan (637), superior grand general became superior protector of the army and grand general became protector of the army; the rest were unchanged, and this system remains in use to the present day.

sentences.zh: 永微已後，以國初勳名與散官名同，年月既久，漸相錯亂。

translations.literal: After Yonghui, because early dynasty merit titles shared names with prestige offices, as years passed they gradually became confused.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yonghui era, because early Tang merit titles shared names with prestige offices, the two categories gradually became confused over the years.

sentences.zh: 咸亨五年三月，更下詔申明，各以類相比。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year of Xianheng, an edict was again issued clarifying that each should be compared by category.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifth year of Xianheng (674), an edict was again issued clarifying how each category should be matched.

sentences.zh: 武德初光祿大夫比今日上柱國，左光祿大夫比柱國，右光祿大夫及上大將軍比上護軍，金紫光祿大夫及將軍比護軍，銀青光祿大夫及上開府比上輕車都尉，正議大夫及開府比輕車都尉，通議大夫及上儀同三司比上騎都尉，朝請大夫及儀同比騎都尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude, master of splendid happiness corresponded to today's upper pillar of the state; left master of splendid happiness to pillar of the state; right master of splendid happiness and superior grand general to superior protector of the army; gold-seal master of splendid happiness and general to protector of the army; silver-seal master of splendid happiness and superior open-the-feudal-office to superior commandant of light chariots; regular counsel master and open-the-feudal-office to commandant of light chariots; communication counsel master and superior equal in ceremony with the three dukes to superior commandant of cavalry; court invitation master and equal in ceremony with the three dukes to commandant of cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wude, master of splendid happiness corresponded to today's upper pillar of the state; the left master of splendid happiness to pillar of the state; the right master of splendid happiness and superior grand general to superior protector of the army; the gold-seal master of splendid happiness and general to protector of the army; the silver-seal master and superior open-the-feudal-office to superior commandant of light chariots; regular counsel master and open-the-feudal-office to commandant of light chariots; communication counsel master and superior equal in ceremony with the three dukes to superior commandant of cavalry; and court invitation master and equal in ceremony with the three dukes to commandant of cavalry.

sentences.zh: 授勳者動盈萬計，每年納課，亦分番於兵部及本郡當上省司。

translations.literal: Those granted merit titles often numbered in the tens of thousands; each year they paid dues and also rotated duty at the Ministry of War and their home commandery, reporting to provincial offices.
translations.idiomatic: Those granted merit titles often numbered in the tens of thousands; each year they paid dues and also rotated through duty at the Ministry of War and their home commandery, reporting to the provincial offices.

sentences.zh: 又分支諸曹，身應役使，有類僮僕，據令乃與公卿齊班，論實在於胥吏之下。

translations.literal: They were also assigned to various bureaus, personally performing corvée service like household servants; by regulation they stood in procession with dukes and ministers, but in reality they ranked below clerks.
translations.idiomatic: They were also assigned to various bureaus and personally performed corvée service like household servants; by regulation they stood in procession with dukes and ministers, but in reality they ranked below the clerks.

sentences.zh: 蓋以其猥多，又出自兵卒，所以然也。

translations.literal: This was because they were numerous and base, and also because they came from common soldiers — that is why it was so.
translations.idiomatic: This was because they were so numerous and low in status, and because they came from the ranks of common soldiers.

sentences.zh: 武德初，以諸道軍務事繁，分置行台尚書省。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude, because military affairs in the various circuits were numerous and complex, mobile terrace departments of state affairs were established separately.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wude, because military affairs in the various circuits were numerous and complex, mobile departments of state affairs were established in the field.

sentences.zh: 其陝東道大行台尚書省，令一人，掌管內軍人，總判省事。

translations.literal: For the great mobile terrace department of state affairs of the Shandong East Circuit, one director oversaw internal military personnel and judged all office affairs in chief.
translations.idiomatic: The great mobile department of state affairs for the Shandong East Circuit had one director who oversaw internal military personnel and had chief authority over all office affairs.

sentences.zh: 僕射一人，掌貳令事。

translations.literal: One vice director assisted the director in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One vice director assisted the director.

sentences.zh: 左丞一人，右丞一人，掌分司糾正省內。

translations.literal: One left and one right assistant divided duties and corrected matters within the department.
translations.idiomatic: One left and one right assistant divided duties and corrected matters within the department.

sentences.zh: 都事一人，主事四人，並掌同京省。

translations.literal: One chief clerk and four clerks — all with duties the same as the capital department.
translations.idiomatic: One chief clerk and four clerks, with duties identical to those of the capital department.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書一人，兼掌吏部事。

translations.literal: One Minister of War, also overseeing Ministry of Personnel affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One Minister of War, who also oversaw personnel affairs.

sentences.zh: 司勳郎中一人。

translations.literal: One Bureau of Merit director.
translations.idiomatic: One director of the Bureau of Merit.

sentences.zh: 主事一人。

translations.literal: One clerk.
translations.idiomatic: One clerk.

sentences.zh: 考功郎中一人，主事一人。

translations.literal: One Merit Review director and one clerk.
translations.idiomatic: One director of merit review and one clerk.

sentences.zh: 兵部郎中一人，主事二人。

translations.literal: One War Bureau director and two clerks.
translations.idiomatic: One war bureau director and two clerks.

sentences.zh: 駕部郎中一人，主事二人。

translations.literal: One Transport Bureau director and two clerks.
translations.idiomatic: One transport bureau director and two clerks.

sentences.zh: 民部尚書一人，兼掌禮部事。

translations.literal: One Minister of the People, also overseeing Ministry of Rites affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One Minister of the People, who also oversaw rites affairs.

sentences.zh: 禮部郎中一人，主事一人。

translations.literal: One Rites Bureau director and one clerk.
translations.idiomatic: One rites bureau director and one clerk.

sentences.zh: 膳部郎中一人，主事一人。

translations.literal: One Provisions Bureau director and one clerk.
translations.idiomatic: One provisions bureau director and one clerk.

sentences.zh: 度支郎中一人，主事二人。

translations.literal: One Revenue Bureau director and two clerks.
translations.idiomatic: One revenue bureau director and two clerks.

sentences.zh: 倉部郎中一人，主事二人。

translations.literal: One Granaries Bureau director and two clerks.
translations.idiomatic: One granaries bureau director and two clerks.

sentences.zh: 工部郎中一人，主事一人。

translations.literal: One Works Bureau director and one clerk.
translations.idiomatic: One works bureau director and one clerk.

sentences.zh: 屯田郎中一人，主事一人。

translations.literal: One Colonies Bureau director and one clerk.
translations.idiomatic: One colonies bureau director and one clerk.

sentences.zh: 每郎中兼京省二司。

translations.literal: Each director also held two bureaus in the capital department.
translations.idiomatic: Each director also concurrently held two bureaus in the capital department.

sentences.zh: 食貨監一人，掌膳羞、財物、賓客、鋪設、音樂、醫藥事，丞二人。

translations.literal: One Food and Goods directorate, overseeing delicacies, property, guests, furnishings, music, and medicine — two assistants.
translations.idiomatic: One food and goods directorate oversaw delicacies, property, guests, furnishings, music, and medicine, with two assistants.

sentences.zh: 農圃監一人，掌倉廩、園圃、柴炭、芻槁、運漕之事，丞四人。

translations.literal: One Farms and Gardens directorate, overseeing granaries, gardens, firewood and charcoal, fodder, and transport of tribute grain — four assistants.
translations.idiomatic: One farms and gardens directorate oversaw granaries, gardens, fuel, fodder, and tribute grain transport, with four assistants.

sentences.zh: 武器監一人，掌兵仗、廄牧之事，丞二人。

translations.literal: One Weapons directorate, overseeing arms and stables and pasturage — two assistants.
translations.idiomatic: One weapons directorate oversaw arms and stables and pasturage, with two assistants.

sentences.zh: 百工監一人，掌舟車及營造雜作之事，丞四人。

translations.literal: One Hundred Crafts directorate, overseeing boats, carriages, construction, and miscellaneous works — four assistants.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred crafts directorate oversaw boats, carriages, construction, and miscellaneous works, with four assistants.

sentences.zh: 諸道行台尚書省令一人，掌同陝東道大行台。

translations.literal: For mobile terrace departments of state affairs in the various circuits, one director with duties the same as the Shandong East great mobile terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Each circuit's mobile department had one director with duties matching those of the Shandong East great mobile terrace.

sentences.zh: 僕射一人，丞一人，都事二人，主事二人。

translations.literal: One vice director, one assistant, two chief clerks, and two clerks.
translations.idiomatic: One vice director, one assistant, two chief clerks, and two clerks.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書一人，兼掌吏部、禮部事。

translations.literal: One Minister of War, also overseeing Ministry of Personnel and Ministry of Rites affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One Minister of War, who also oversaw personnel and rites affairs.

sentences.zh: 考功郎中一人。

translations.literal: One Merit Review director.
translations.idiomatic: One director of merit review.

sentences.zh: 主事二人。

translations.literal: Two clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Two clerks.

sentences.zh: 膳部郎中一人，主事二人。

translations.literal: One Provisions Bureau director and two clerks.
translations.idiomatic: One provisions bureau director and two clerks.

sentences.zh: 兵部郎中二人，主事二人。

translations.literal: Two War Bureau directors and two clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Two war bureau directors and two clerks.

sentences.zh: 民部尚書一人，兼掌刑部、工部。

translations.literal: One Minister of the People, also overseeing Ministry of Punishments and Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: One Minister of the People, who also oversaw punishments and works.

sentences.zh: 倉部郎中二人，主事二人。

translations.literal: Two Granaries Bureau directors and two clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Two granaries bureau directors and two clerks.

sentences.zh: 刑部郎中一人，主事二人。

translations.literal: One Punishments Bureau director and two clerks.
translations.idiomatic: One punishments bureau director and two clerks.

sentences.zh: 屯田郎中一人，主事二人。

translations.literal: One Colonies Bureau director and two clerks.
translations.idiomatic: One colonies bureau director and two clerks.

sentences.zh: 食貨監一人，兼掌農圃監事，丞一人。

translations.literal: One Food and Goods directorate, also overseeing Farms and Gardens affairs — one assistant.
translations.idiomatic: One food and goods directorate also oversaw farms and gardens affairs, with one assistant.

sentences.zh: 兼掌百工監事，丞二人。

translations.literal: Also overseeing Hundred Crafts affairs — two assistants.
translations.idiomatic: It also oversaw hundred crafts affairs, with two assistants.

sentences.zh: 時秦王、齊王府官之外，又各置左右六護軍府及左右親事帳內府。

translations.literal: At that time, apart from the offices of the Prince of Qin and Prince of Qi, left and right six protector-of-the-army offices and left and right personal-attendant inner-account offices were also established on each side.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, besides the staffs of the Princes of Qin and Qi, each prince also had left and right sets of six protector-of-the-army offices and personal-attendant inner-account offices.

sentences.zh: 其左一右一護軍府護軍各一人，掌率統軍已下侍衛陪從。

translations.literal: For the left-first and right-first protector-of-the-army offices, one protector of the army each commanded army commanders and below in guard attendance and escort.
translations.idiomatic: The left-first and right-first protector-of-the-army offices each had one protector who commanded army commanders and below in guard attendance and escort.

sentences.zh: 副護軍各二人。

translations.literal: Two deputy protectors of the army each.
translations.idiomatic: Each had two deputy protectors of the army.

sentences.zh: 長史各一人。

translations.literal: One chief aide each.
translations.idiomatic: One chief aide each.

sentences.zh: 錄事參軍各一人。

translations.literal: One recording adjutant each.
translations.idiomatic: One recording adjutant each.

sentences.zh: 倉曹參軍事各一人，兵曹參軍事各一人，鎧曹參軍事各一人。

translations.literal: One granary bureau adjutant, one military bureau adjutant, and one armor bureau adjutant each.
translations.idiomatic: Each had one granary bureau adjutant, one military bureau adjutant, and one armor bureau adjutant.

sentences.zh: 統軍各五人，別將各十人，分掌領親勳衛及外軍。

translations.literal: Five army commanders and ten separate commanders each, dividing command of the personal, merit, and wing guards and external armies.
translations.idiomatic: Each office had five army commanders and ten separate commanders, who divided command of the personal, merit, and wing guards and the external armies.

sentences.zh: 左二右二護軍府、左三右三護軍府，各減統軍三人，別將六人。

translations.literal: The left-second, right-second, left-third, and right-third protector-of-the-army offices each had three fewer army commanders and six fewer separate commanders.
translations.idiomatic: The left-second, right-second, left-third, and right-third protector-of-the-army offices each had three fewer army commanders and six fewer separate commanders.

sentences.zh: 余職員同左一右一府。

translations.literal: The remaining staff matched the left-first and right-first offices.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining staff matched those of the left-first and right-first offices.

sentences.zh: 其左右親事府統軍各一人，掌率左右別將、侍衛陪從。

translations.literal: For the left and right personal-attendant offices, one army commander each commanded the left and right separate commanders in guard attendance and escort.
translations.idiomatic: The left and right personal-attendant offices each had one army commander who led the left and right separate commanders in guard attendance and escort.

sentences.zh: 長史一人。

translations.literal: One chief aide.
translations.idiomatic: One chief aide.

sentences.zh: 錄事參軍事各一人。

translations.literal: One recording adjutant each.
translations.idiomatic: One recording adjutant each.

sentences.zh: 兵曹參軍事各一人，鎧曹參軍事各一人。

translations.literal: One military bureau adjutant and one armor bureau adjutant each.
translations.idiomatic: Each had one military bureau adjutant and one armor bureau adjutant.

sentences.zh: 左別將各一人，右別將各一人。

translations.literal: One left separate commander and one right separate commander each.
translations.idiomatic: Each side had one left and one right separate commander.

sentences.zh: 掌率親事以上侍衛陪從。

translations.literal: They commanded personal attendants and above in guard attendance and escort.
translations.idiomatic: They commanded personal attendants and above in guard attendance and escort.

sentences.zh: 其帳內府職員品秩，與統軍府同。

translations.literal: The staff grades and ranks of the inner-account offices were the same as the army commander offices.
translations.idiomatic: The staff grades and ranks of the inner-account offices were the same as those of the army commander offices.

sentences.zh: 又有庫直及驅咥直。

translations.literal: There were also armory duty officers and drive duty officers.
translations.idiomatic: There were also armory duty officers and drive duty officers.

sentences.zh: 各於左右內選才堪者，量事置之。

translations.literal: From the left and right sides, men of suitable talent were selected and placed according to the needs of each task.
translations.idiomatic: Talented men were selected from the left and right staffs and assigned according to the needs of each task.

sentences.zh: 武德四年，太宗平洛陽之後，又置天策上將府官員。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, after the Taizong pacified Luoyang, staff for the Heavenly Stratagem General-in-Chief Office was also established.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Wude (621), after Emperor Taizong pacified Luoyang, staff for the Heavenly Stratagem General-in-Chief Office was also established.

sentences.zh: 天策上將一人，掌國之征討，總判府事。

translations.literal: One Heavenly Stratagem General-in-Chief directed the state's campaigns and judged all office affairs in chief.
translations.idiomatic: One Heavenly Stratagem General-in-Chief directed the state's military campaigns and had chief authority over all office affairs.

sentences.zh: 長史、司馬各一人，從事中郎二人，並掌通判府事。

translations.literal: One chief aide and one administrative aide, and two attendant gentlemen — all with general authority over office affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One chief aide, one administrative aide, and two attendant gentlemen all shared general authority over office affairs.

sentences.zh: 軍諮祭酒二人，謀軍事，贊相禮儀，宴接賓客。

translations.literal: Two military counsel libationers planned military affairs, assisted in ritual etiquette, and received guests at banquets.
translations.idiomatic: Two military counsel libationers planned military affairs, assisted in ritual etiquette, and received guests at banquets.

sentences.zh: 典簽四人，掌宣傳導引之事。

translations.literal: Four protocol secretaries directed proclamation, transmission, and guidance.
translations.idiomatic: Four protocol secretaries handled proclamation, transmission, and guidance.

sentences.zh: 主簿二人，掌省復教命。

translations.literal: Two registrars reviewed and returned edicts and orders.
translations.idiomatic: Two registrars reviewed and returned edicts and orders.

sentences.zh: 錄事二人，記室參軍事二人，掌書疏表啟，宣行教命。

translations.literal: Two recorders and two secretariat adjutants managed documents, memorials, and reports, and proclaimed and executed orders.
translations.idiomatic: Two recorders and two secretariat adjutants managed documents, memorials, and reports, and proclaimed and executed orders.

sentences.zh: 功曹參軍事二人，掌官員假使、儀式、醫藥、選舉、考課、祿恤、鋪設等事。

translations.literal: Two merit bureau adjutants managed temporary assignments of officials, ceremonies, medicine, selection, merit review, salary and condolence payments, and furnishings.
translations.idiomatic: Two merit bureau adjutants managed temporary official assignments, ceremonies, medicine, selection, merit review, salary and condolence payments, and furnishings.

sentences.zh: 倉曹參軍二人，掌糧廩、公廨、田園、廚膳、過所等事。

translations.literal: Two granary bureau adjutants managed grain stores, government offices, gardens, kitchens, and travel permits.
translations.idiomatic: Two granary bureau adjutants managed grain stores, government offices, gardens, kitchens, and travel permits.

sentences.zh: 兵曹參軍事二人，掌兵士簿帳、差點等事。

translations.literal: Two military bureau adjutants managed soldiers' registers and assignments.
translations.idiomatic: Two military bureau adjutants managed soldiers' registers and assignments.

sentences.zh: 騎曹參軍事二人，掌馬驢雜畜簿帳及牧養支料草粟等事。

translations.literal: Two cavalry bureau adjutants managed registers of horses, donkeys, and miscellaneous livestock, and pasturage, fodder, and grain supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Two cavalry bureau adjutants managed registers of horses, donkeys, and other livestock, along with pasturage, fodder, and grain supplies.

sentences.zh: 鎧曹參軍事二人，掌戎仗之事。

translations.literal: Two armor bureau adjutants managed military equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Two armor bureau adjutants managed military equipment.

sentences.zh: 士曹參軍事二人，掌營造及罪罰之事。

translations.literal: Two works bureau adjutants managed construction and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Two works bureau adjutants managed construction and punishments.

sentences.zh: 參軍事六人，掌出使及雜檢校之事。

translations.literal: Six adjutants managed missions abroad and miscellaneous inspections.
translations.idiomatic: Six adjutants managed missions abroad and miscellaneous inspections.

sentences.zh: 其陝東道大行台尚書令及天策上將，太宗在籓為之。

translations.literal: The Shandong East great mobile terrace director and Heavenly Stratagem General-in-Chief were held by Taizong while he was still a prince.
translations.idiomatic: The Shandong East great mobile terrace director and Heavenly Stratagem General-in-Chief were held by Taizong while he was still a prince.

sentences.zh: 及升儲，並省之。

translations.literal: When he was elevated as heir apparent, both were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When he was elevated as heir apparent, both offices were abolished.

sentences.zh: 山東道行台，武德五年省。

translations.literal: The Shandong Circuit mobile terrace was abolished in the fifth year of Wude.
translations.idiomatic: The Shandong Circuit mobile terrace was abolished in the fifth year of Wude (622).

sentences.zh: 餘道九年省。

translations.literal: The remaining circuits were abolished in the ninth year.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining circuit mobile terraces were abolished in the ninth year (626).
